issues.title: Bloom filter probe: hash+lookup only run heads of equal consecutive keys
issues.hypothesis: Warm profile of q21 (3rd run in the same process, JSON profiling): the l2 and l3 lineitem scans carry `optional: l_orderkey IN BF(l_orderkey)` and cost 0.72s and 0.86s CPU for 60M rows each. A plain warm 2-column scan of the same columns costs 0.18s CPU, and hashing 60M BIGINTs costs about 0.15s (EXPLAIN ANALYZE bit_xor(hash(l_orderkey))). So about 0.4-0.5s per scan is hashing plus random BF lookups: 708K keys give a 2MB filter, which misses L2. That is about 1.2s of the query's ~4.7s CPU. lineitem is clustered on the join key (about 4 consecutive rows per key), so most hash/lookup work repeats the previous row's. If BFTableFilter::Filter checks whether key[i]==key[i-1] and reuses the previous result, hashing and lookups drop about 4x on clustered data.
issues.plan: In src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp, BFTableFilter::Filter: add a fast path when keys_v is a FLAT_VECTOR, its physical type is a fixed-width integer (INT8..INT64, UINT8..UINT64; a template over T), and it has no NULLs in the approved rows (validity AllValid, or a cheap per-row check). Steps: (1) walk the approved rows (through sel if set, otherwise 0..count-1) and write the positions where key != previous approved key into a head selection (state.bf_sel or a new buffer in BFTableFilterState, src/include/duckdb/planner/table_filter_state.hpp). (2) If heads > ~3/4 of approved_tuple_count, fall back to the existing path, so unclustered data pays only one compare per row. (3) Otherwise slice keys_v by the head sel, run VectorOperations::Hash on the heads only, and call filter.LookupOne per head (or LookupHashes). (4) Walk the approved rows again, carrying the current head's found flag, and compact sel / approved_tuple_count the way the current code does (keep the existing semantics: sel.Initialize(bf_sel) when sel was not set, otherwise remap). Results are identical to the per-row path because equal keys hash identically. Do not touch BloomFilter itself.
issues.expected_gain: q21: l2+l3 scans 1.58s → ~0.8s CPU, out of ~4.7s total CPU. Roughly -8..-15% wall. Also l1-type scans if a BF is ever pushed on a clustered key.
issues.generality: Helps any join-filter BF probe on a column stored clustered or sorted by the join key, which is common for fact tables loaded in key order (lineitem/orders, events by id, time-sorted data): semi joins, delim joins, FK joins with selective build sides. Unclustered columns pay one extra compare per row plus the fallback check, under 0.5ns/row.
issues.risk: Low. Results are unchanged by construction. The main correctness hazards are NULL handling (fall back when any NULL is present) and sel remapping. Edge risk: the adaptive fallback threshold is wrong for data that alternates between clustered and not, costing a small amount of extra work.

dispatch: Bloom filter probe: hash+lookup only run heads of equal consecutive keys
output.memory:
## Planner memory (q21 specialisation run)

## Tooling facts
- dbe-tool profile / sql output is truncated (~150 lines / by width).
- **Every `dbe-tool sql` call is a FRESH PROCESS with a cold buffer pool.** The first scan of a column in a call reads from disk/OS cache
  and is 5-10x slower. Older "scan cost" numbers in my notes were COLD and wrong. Always warm up in the same call first.
- Full warm profile recipe (works): one sql call with `CREATE TEMP TABLE w AS <q>; CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE w AS <q>; PRAGMA enable_profiling='json';
  SET profiling_output='/home/shresth/dev/db_evolve/work/slots/slot0/.dbe/p.json'; CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE w AS <q>; PRAGMA disable_profiling;`
  then a second call: `SELECT trim(line) FROM (SELECT unnest(string_split(content, chr(10))) line FROM read_text('<path>')) WHERE line SIMILAR TO
  '.*(operator_name|operator_timing|operator_cardinality|"latency|Filters|Join Type|Conditions).*'` (use head/tail to see both halves).
- Shell variables in commands are blocked ("can't be checked"), and so is `$(...)`. Write the literal query out.
- `EXPLAIN (FORMAT json)` times out. Operator timings are summed CPU across threads; latency is wall.

## Warm facts (SF10, 8 threads)
- lineitem cols are BitPacking. A warm 60M-row scan is ~0.1s CPU per int column; 3 cols + col-col filter 0.24s. Hash(BIGINT) on 60M rows = 0.15s CPU.
- Warm q21 latency 0.82s, ~4.7s CPU total. Operator CPU: l1 scan 0.33 (min/max only, no BF), FILTER 0.12, suppkey join 0.27,
  orders scan (status='F' + BF) 0.30, orders⋈l1 join 0.38, RIGHT_DELIM_JOIN 0.26, LEFT_DELIM 0.08,
  l2 scan (BF on l_orderkey) 0.72 → 3.56M rows, l2 inner join 0.38, l3 scan (BF) 0.86 → 3.53M, l3 FILTER 0.08, l3 join 0.33,
  anti HASH_JOIN 0.30, delim HASH_GROUP_BYs 0.03-0.05, final agg 0.02.
- The current best build ALREADY pushes BF(l_orderkey) into the l2/l3 scans and the orders scan. The BF probe costs ~0.4-0.5s CPU per
  60M rows (2MB filter, random access). This is now the single biggest fixable cost.
- lineitem is clustered by l_orderkey (~4 rows/key), which motivates run-dedupe of BF probes (dispatched in round 4).

## Codebase facts
- Optimizer order: BUILD_SIDE_PROBE_SIDE (optimizer.cpp:247) before JOIN_FILTER_PUSHDOWN (:320).
- GenerateJoinFilters (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp ~210) skips LEFT/OUTER/ANTI/RIGHT_ANTI/RIGHT_SEMI/MARK/SINGLE. The q21 subquery
  joins are INNER (lineitem probe ⋈ DELIM_SCAN build, orderkey= AND suppkey<>). The RIGHT_SEMI/ANTI are the delim joins themselves.
- BF gate: CanUseBloomFilter physical_hash_join.cpp:~761. BF impl: src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp (1 64-bit sector, 4 bits/key,
  12 bits/key sizing; BFTableFilter::Filter hashes approved rows → LookupHashes → remap sel). Scan dispatch: column_segment.cpp:558.
- Optional min/max filters: zonemap-only. The optional BF IS evaluated per row.
- Perfect HJ: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp, MAX_BUILD_SIZE 1,048,576.

## History
- E0001 RETIRED: BF for 1-equality + non-eq conds, DELIM_GET build → official ~0%.
- E0002 RETIRED: BF for sparse perfect HJ (l1 suppkey) — BF hashing cost > savings. Bad idea for low-selectivity BF on a cheap scan.
- E0003 RETIRED: join filters for RIGHT_SEMI/ANTI — misread plan; BF on l2/l3 is ~0% net because the BF probe cost ≈ the join work saved.
  Lesson: the cost of the BF probe itself is the problem. Make the probe cheaper rather than adding more BFs.
- Round 4: dispatched "Bloom filter probe: hash+lookup only run heads of equal consecutive keys".

## Ideas for later
- If run-dedupe works: also skip the BF for vectors whose zonemap range is fully covered? (no; keys are spread). Exact bitmap filter for
  dense integer key sets (key-min bit test, no hash), useful when the build key range is < ~64x the key count.
- Subquery inner joins: 0.33-0.38s CPU for 3.5M probe rows (~100ns/row): chains of build rows per orderkey plus residual suppkey<>. Investigate.
- orders⋈l1 join 0.38s for 712K probe / 1.52M build. Build-side cost?
- Big/risky: rewrite EXISTS/NOT EXISTS (k= AND s<>) as per-key aggregates; share the l2/l3 scans.
